claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.9, annual return 5%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.85 to 1.79 (change -0.06).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.85 to 1.85. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.49 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.85); it breaks even at 30.6 bps with daily turnover 0.07.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.85 against 1.85 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 1.32 against 1.85 in research, a gap of +0.53.
The best year gives 25% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 77%; Sharpe is 2.1 in calm and 1.42 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 1.90 becomes 1.90 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.21 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.53).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.85 to as low as 1.67 (as low as 1.69 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 36% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 23% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
